theorem_title: Shao's Lemma 2.2: the asymmetric averaging inequality
natural_language_statement:
Let $n$ be even with $n \ge 10$ and let $a$, $b$, $c$ each be decreasing sequences of $n$ reals in $[0,1]$, with averages $A$, $B$ and $C$. Suppose that for every triple of indices $i, j, k$ with $i + j + k \ge n$ we have

$$a_i b_j + b_j c_k + c_k a_i \le \tfrac{5}{8}(a_i + b_j + c_k).$$

Then $AB + BC + CA \le \frac{5}{8}(A + B + C)$.

This three-sequence version of Lemma 2.1 lets the induction split a function into three different fibers rather than three copies of one.
source: Xuancheng Shao, "A density version of the Vinogradov three primes theorem", Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 489-512, arXiv:1206.6139v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6139, Lemma 2.2
